sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant- claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the award dated 24.04.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambah, District Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 133/2010, whereby compensation of Rs.4,79,000/- along with interest was awarded in favour of the claimant.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambah, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present appeal has been filed seeking enhancement of the compensation amount.
2. The date of the accident, negligence of the offending vehicle and liability of the insurer are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality and are not under challenge.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the impugned award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal is illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the evidence available on record.

It is submitted that despite clear and unrebutted NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10657 2 MA-731-2013 documentary as well as oral evidence showing that the appellant was earning Rs.1,80,000/- per annum from his business as a milk seller, the learned Tribunal wrongly assessed his income at only Rs.36,000/- per annum.
The appellant had filed Articles A, B and C to substantiate his business and income.

It is further submitted that although the learned Tribunal accepted that the appellant suffered grievous injuries resulting in complete amputation of the right leg below the knee with 70%
permanent disability, it committed an error in assessing the loss of earning capacity at only 50%,

1 whereas due to functional disability the appellant has become totally incapable of performing his work and the loss of earning capacity ought to have been assessed at 100%.

Learned counsel for the appellant placed reliance on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Indra Bai vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and another, reported in 2023 ACJ 1473, and submitted that in the said case, where a labourer suffered 40% permanent disability, the Apex Court assessed his permanent disability in relation to income as 100%.
4.

entities.text: Indra Bai vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and another, reported in 2023 ACJ 1473
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further submitted by counsel for the appellant that the learned Tribunal committed a grave error in not awarding separate compensation for permanent disability, in awarding only Rs.1,25,000/- against actual medical and related expenses of Rs.5,00,000/-, and in granting inadequate amounts towards pain and suffering, attendant charges and loss of amenities,
considering the nature of injuries and their lifelong impact on the appellant.
It is also submitted that the Claims Tribunal committed an error in not granting any addition towards future prospects.

Learned counsel for the appellant placed reliance on the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10657 3 MA-731-2013 Lalan D. and another vs.
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. , reported in 2020 ACJ 2517, and Nur Ahamad Abdulsab Kanavi vs.
Abdul Munaf and others , reported in 2025 ACJ 1621 .

sentences.text: Accordingly, learned counsel prays that the impugned award be suitably modified by enhancing the compensation under all relevant heads along with appropriate interest.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company opposed the contentions raised on behalf of the appellant and submitted that the award passed by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any interference.
Accordingly, dismissal of the appeal has been prayed for.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
On perusal of the record, it is found that the appellant met with an accident and, due to the said accident, his right leg below the knee was amputated.
The appellant filed a permanent disability certificate (Ex.P-136), wherein the concerned Doctor assessed his permanent disability as 70%.
However, the appellant did not examine the Doctor who issued the permanent disability certificate.
As per Schedule I, Part II of the Workmen's Compensation Act, amputation below the knee is assessed at 50% permanent disability.

8. So far as the contention of the appellant regarding assessment of permanent disability in relation to income being on the lower side is concerned, it is found that the appellant was purchasing and selling milk and was working with two employees.
Thus, he cannot be treated as a labourer.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10657 4 MA-731-2013
Therefore, his permanent disability in relation to income cannot be assessed as 100%.
Consequently, the judgment relied upon by learned counsel for the appellant in this regard is not applicable to the facts of the present case and does not advance his case.

Considering the evidence on record, the nature of permanent disability and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in Paragraphs 12, 13 and 14 of the impugned award, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal has rightly Dileep Sharma vs Veerendra Verma on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165592108/
2 assessed the loss of earning capacity at 50% and no interference is warranted on this aspect.
9.

As regards the submission advanced on behalf of the appellant concerning the assessment of his income, on careful scrutiny of the evidence available on record, it emerges that the appellant did not possess any licence for purchasing or selling milk.

In the absence of such licence and in the absence of any cogent and reliable documentary evidence to substantiate the claim that the appellant was working as a milk seller and, therefore, his income was not duly proved.

Therefore, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in Paragraph 17 of the impugned award on this aspect are found to be just, proper and based on correct appreciation of evidence, and hence do not warrant any interference by this Court.
10. However, it is noticed that the accident occurred on 11.10.2010.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sukhdevi vs. Devendra Kumar, ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi vs. Bansal Roadway , 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Company Limited vs. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134, it has been held that in absence of documentary proof of income, the income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10657 5 MA-731-2013
Accordingly, this Court deems it appropriate to assess the income of the claimant as that of an unskilled worker.
Thus, his monthly income is assessed at Rs.4,145/- per month as per the Minimum Wages Act.

11. So far as future prospects are concerned, in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimant is entitled to future prospects at the rate of 40%.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, as per the decision of the Apex Court in the case o f Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, (2009) 6 SCC 121,
considering the age of the claimant, an appropriate multiplier of 18 has rightly been applied by the Claims Tribunal.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant- claimant and the extent of permanent disability suffered by him in the accident in question, this Court is of the considered opinion that total compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- under the conventional heads, namely special diet, transportation, pain and suffering and other incidental expenses, would be just and proper.

13. Accordingly, the claimant is entitled to receive the compensation amount under the following heads:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Income Rs. 4145 x 12= Rs. 4

After adding Future Prospects @40% Rs. 69636/-
 Permanent Disability 50 % Rs. 34818/-
 Multiplier 18 Rs.626724/-
Other Heads:- Rs.2,50,000/-
Total compensation = Rs.8,76,724/-

3  NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10657  6  11.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.8,76,724/- as against the sum of Rs.4,79,000/-
awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellant- claimant is held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs. 3,97,724/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
12. Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed and impugned award is modified.
The compensation is enhanced by Rs. 3,97,724/- and enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of depositing of Court fee.
All other conditions imposed by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

13. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the claimant- appellant shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
14. In view of the foregoing, the miscellaneous appeal stands partly allowed and is disposed of accordingly.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
